quick: Myoclonus 7.2 g/day initial, up to 24 g/day divided
With or without food; with liquid
No adjustment for isolated hepatic impairment
Renal function; coagulation in at-risk patients
summary: Piracetam is a cyclic GABA-derivative pyrrolidone marketed as a nootropic and used (per EMA/SmPC and BNF) chiefly for adjunctive treatment of cortical myoclonus, and in some countries for vertigo and age-related cognitive decline. It is renally eliminated and requires dose reduction in renal impairment. Evidence for cognitive indications is limited and it is not FDA-approved.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of vertigo (per local labels)
Adjunct in age-associated cognitive impairment / dementia (where licensed)
Dyslexia in children as adjunct to other measures (where licensed)

dosage.d: Initial 7.2 g/day; increase by 4.8 g/day every 3-4 days up to 24 g/day in 2-3 divided doses
dosage.n: Reduce other antimyoclonic drugs as tolerated

dosage.d: CrCl 50-79: 2/3 dose; 30-49: 1/3 dose; <30 or dialysis: avoid/contraindicated per label

admin: Take orally with or without food, swallowing tablets with liquid; oral solution can be taken in water or juice
Divide the total daily dose into 2-3 administrations
Titrate gradually in myoclonus and review the need for other antimyoclonic agents
Do not stop abruptly in myoclonus; taper to avoid recurrence or withdrawal myoclonus
moa: Piracetam is a cyclic derivative of GABA whose precise mechanism is not fully defined. It is thought to act on neuronal and erythrocyte membranes, improving membrane fluidity, and to modulate neurotransmission (including AMPA/glutamatergic and cholinergic systems) and enhance microcirculation by reducing platelet aggregation and red-cell rigidity. These effects are proposed to underlie its neuroprotective, antimyoclonic and rheological actions.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to piracetam, other pyrrolidone derivatives, or excipients
relative: Impaired hemostasis, major surgery, or risk of bleeding

preg: Not FDA-approved; piracetam crosses the placenta. Avoid during pregnancy unless clearly necessary and only under medical supervision.
lact: Piracetam is excreted in human breast milk. Breastfeeding should be discontinued during treatment or the drug avoided.
renal: Piracetam is eliminated essentially unchanged by the kidneys, so dose reduction is required in renal impairment based on creatinine clearance (approximately two-thirds dose for CrCl 50-79, one-third for 30-49 mL/min) and it should be avoided or is contraindicated in severe impairment/end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required for isolated hepatic impairment, as elimination is predominantly renal.

moderate: Anticoagulants/antiplatelets (warfarin, aspirin) - additive antiplatelet effect and bleeding risk
Thyroid hormone (T3/T4) - reports of confusion, irritability and sleep disturbance with concurrent use
minor: Other nootropic/CNS-active agents - additive effects (limited data)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference documented.

monitoring: Renal function before and during therapy, particularly in the elderly and on high doses
Signs of bleeding or bruising in patients with hemostatic risk or on anticoagulants
counsel: Take the divided doses as prescribed; do not stop suddenly if treated for myoclonus
Report easy bruising or bleeding, especially if you take blood thinners
Tell your doctor about kidney problems - the dose may need adjusting
Report marked restlessness, low mood or sleep disturbance
pk: Symptomatic effect over days to weeks of dosing
Dosed two to three times daily
Store below 25-30 C in a dry place
pearls: Not FDA-approved; pending clinical review. Licensed in Europe (EMA/SmPC) mainly for cortical myoclonus.
Almost entirely renally cleared - always dose-adjust for kidney function and avoid in severe impairment
Inhibits platelet aggregation - use caution before surgery and with anticoagulants
Do not stop abruptly in myoclonus to avoid withdrawal myoclonus/seizures
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue the regular schedule; do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose experience is limited; reported effects include bloody diarrhea and abdominal pain at very high doses. There is no specific antidote. Manage with supportive and symptomatic care, gastric emptying or lavage if recent; hemodialysis can remove piracetam (extraction ~50-60%) and may be used in severe overdose or renal failure.
